items.title: Show HN: Synth Patch Hero
items.description: Show HN: I wanted to be more deliberate and systematic in how I approach working on synth patches. With the help of our friend Claude, I put together a game that runs through exercises that builds that muscle in a fun and approachable way where you learn as you build patches on a modular rack. I do not have a Eurorack, nor a strong desire to own one (yet); but I do have a bit of other physical gear. I wanted to see if the lessons would translate to boxes, where sound is also better than the browser. So I have started adding groove box specific enhanced lessons (so far just a couple for the Digitone II, but they worked so far). Also: - You can set up MIDI in settings and play your patch in the browser with a MIDI keyboard (Chrome worked, but Safari didn't when I tried). - The Help in the exercises can unblock you when you get stuck and teach you as it helps. - You can pick a groove box in settings under 'my gear' to get some device-specific lessons.

items.title: Show HN: A narrated map tour of the events leading up to the Texas Revolution
items.description:
Show HN: I put together a narrated map of the Texas Revolution. You can listen to a 20-minute audio guided version or just scroll through the events: I thought the chronological and location based timeline made it easier to follow and learn as well. I was inspired by Mapbox’s “storytelling” template on GitHub and built my own version with MapLibre fork of Mapbox GL (with free satellite imagery and terrain tiles from USGS) and lots of help from Claude. There are lots of parameters that were built in, like the rotation and transition speed. Essentially themed it and added source links to the cards. The information was sourced from Handbook of Texas by THC. The voice is AI generated using Elevenlabs v4. That github project https://github.com/mapbox/storytelling has some cool use-case examples that have been published as web features by a few publications. There is so much more you can do with this, like hooking it to live data. The template is a great place to start! Narrations by Elevenlabs TTS. Working on this new one around Houston Oil industry as well. https://whistlestop.guide/features/houston-oil
Website metadata: Fifteen years, told in 21 places. In 1821 Texas was a remote province of a newly independent Mexico, shared uneasily by Tejanos, Comanche and American colonists. Follow the quarrels, the first shots at Gonzales, the Alamo and Goliad, the long retreat east, and 18 minutes beside the San Jacinto River.

items.title: Show HN: Budget – an open-source private budgeting app for Mac and Windows
items.description:
Show HN: Budget is a free, open-source app for Mac and Windows. With the simple mode, it gives you what you'd expect of a budgeting app: configure budgets and track expenses against those budgets. But, if you're a geek like me and are way too interested in your personal finance, the extended mode offers features like carrying leftover budgets to the next month, splitting expenses across multiple budgets and seeing how much you can freely spend the coming year, while taking into account any large future expenses (like a car insurance where the premium is paid on a yearly basis). This app is the result of a hobby of mine to track my expenses. It started a few years ago in a spreadsheet, but that spreadsheet at some point took me minutes to edit on my MacBook with 8 gigs of RAM. I had the idea to turn it into an app before, but never had the time to do so. I worked in the software industry until halfway through 2024, when LLMs were mostly just used for debugging. But, because of all the positivity I heard about how good they've gotten now, I tried to see if I could turn the spreadsheet into an app with the help of Claude Opus 5.5. I had to point out a couple of bugs and bad decisions (like bad alignment of text and using entire English sentences instead of keywords as keys for translation), but overall, it worked really well. Budgeting apps are of course not new. But, they often are either free but with limited features, free but with an obnoxious amount of cookies and/or ads, free but charge money for important features or charge money to be used at all. The idea of this project is that there are no cookies, no ads, no fees, no data being stored remotely and that the code is open-source. Data ownership stands at the center of the app: you can easily export/import your data and create back-ups (besides the automatic back-ups the app creates for you). It is available to everyone, of course as long as you have a device that is supported (currently only devices that run macOS and Windows). I'm interested to hear if you think this app has any potential and if you think any important features are missing.
Website metadata: A private, local budget app for Mac and Windows. Your data never leaves your computer. - hendrikdemir/budget
items.product_description: A private, local budget app for Mac and Windows. Your data never leaves your computer. - hendrikdemir/budget

items.title: Show HN: Truce – a neutral mediator that AI agents can call to settle disputes
items.description:
Show HN: Hi HN, I'm Frank, founder of Truce. Truce is a neutral AI mediator. Each side tells it their side in private, Truce proposes one specific outcome, and nothing happens unless both people sign. The part that may interest you is the agent side. Truce is a remote MCP server ( https://trucehq.com/mcp ) with 12 tools, so an assistant can start a Truce for its user, or answer one for the other person with their consent. There is also "Agent Truce": two agents acting for different people or companies settle a dispute between themselves, such as a refund, a late delivery or an invoice. Each agent gives its side, its evidence and a private mandate from its human, for example "may pay up to $300". The mediator never sees either mandate, so it proposes on the merits. A proposal that fits inside both mandates is accepted automatically; anything else goes back to the humans. Truce never moves money. It's free for AI agents. One-minute demo on the page. I'd especially like criticism of the mandate design. How would you game it, and what would make you trust it for your own agents?
Website metadata: AI agents can start a Truce or a free Who's right? for their user through Truce's MCP server or JSON API. A human always sends the invite and signs. Agent Truce lets AI agents settle disputes with other agents, within limits their humans set.

items.title: Show HN: SecureVibe – Find and trace vulnerabilities for vibe coded apps
items.description:
Show HN: Hello HN, just wanted to share my project that I've been working on the past months, where I noticed the issue that now we ship faster than setting up the requirements for the project. So I thought of building secureVibe to find vulnerabilities in your codebase. Now I have a MVP where it doesn't just scan the code and show random analysis I used Tree-sitter and AST to understand code context to validate vulnerabilities found as it builds a graph of application routes, handlers and database calls so it helps to determine whether findings are confirmed or likely. Briefly the features: 1- shows all vulnerabilities in your code with code snippets 2-fixing with ai option (optional with your own api key for now) 3- ask the graph feature as you can ask where the attacker can exploit my website or authentication issues (I used graphify as foundation for it ) 4- You can filter vulnerabilities categories (like Cwe, database injection and more) from dashboard and you can download it as html report simple interactive one so you can fix it on your own later. I would love to know your thoughts and feedback to continue on the development on it like some of the problems I faced is benchmarks to validate security rules. With some research I found openssf benchmark so would really appreciate feedback to continue on developing with next phases. It works best with TypeScript
Website metadata: Static security scanning that understands how your code is built, then ranks findings by whether a public route can reach them. 240 rules, 101 CWEs, no account, no AI in detection.

items.title: Show HN: An interactive album that changes with stuff like time and moon phase
items.description:
Show HN: I've made Return to Repeat, an album and a browser music player with ten songs without beginning or end. It has built-in musical variations, some you can control and interact with and some that activate based on things like date, time of day, visit counts and current moon phase. Try the birds on track three for a starting place. Wanted to explore other ways of releasing and experiencing digital music, and perhaps finding a route back to kind of "being" with music. My last release was a cassette in an edition of three, that also came with a minimal web player. It's built mainly with Tone.js on the Web Audio API, with help from Claude (writing code, debugging). The music is composed as (sometimes long) seamless loops, with multiple stems for variations. Didn't want to go the proper app-route, with the main trade-off being no background audio. Also had some trouble with airplay, but think I've managed to get rid of the most obvious bugs. Love to hear what you think of the listening experience! Happy to answer any questions about the project.
Website metadata: I made ten songs, with no beginning and no end. Press play and the first one stays until you ask for the next. Some parts are alive and some will change from time to time.
